Task: Text Content Safety

Write code that applies category thresholds to decide whether to allow text using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Perspective API:
  Service: Perspective API
  SDK: requests
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: comments:analyze
  Setup hints: PERSPECTIVE_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://developers.perspectiveapi.com/s/

Option 2 — Amazon Comprehend Toxicity / Bedrock Guardrails:
  Service: Amazon Comprehend / Bedrock Guardrails
  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: detect_toxic_content, apply_guardrail
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/comprehend/latest/dg/trust-safety.html

Option 3 — Alibaba Content Moderation:
  Service: Alibaba Content Moderation
  SDK: alibabacloud_green
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: text/scan
  Setup hints: ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID, ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/doc-detail/331920.html

Option 4 — Tisane:
  Service: Tisane Text Moderation
  SDK: requests
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: POST /parse
  Setup hints: TISANE_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.tisane.ai/

Option 5 — watsonx guardrails:
  Service: watsonx.ai guardrails / HAP detection
  SDK: ibm-watsonx-ai / REST
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: HAP detection, text detection
  Setup hints: WATSONX_API_KEY, WATSONX_PROJECT_ID
  Official docs: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/watsonxdata/premium/2.3.x?topic=prompts-removing-harmful-content

Option 6 — Azure AI Content Safety:
  Service: Azure AI Content Safety
  SDK: requests / azure-ai-contentsafety
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: analyze_text
  Setup hints: AZURE_CONTENT_SAFETY_ENDPOINT, AZURE_CONTENT_SAFETY_KEY
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-safety/overview

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

import os
import requests

def allow_text(text_content: str, category_thresholds: dict) -> bool:
<GAP>
    api_key = os.environ.get("PERSPECTIVE_API_KEY")
    if not api_key:
        raise ValueError("PERSPECTIVE_API_KEY environment variable not set.")

    # Perspective API endpoint
    analyze_url = "https://commentanalyzer.googleapis.com/v1alpha1/comments:analyze"

    # Construct the request payload
    # Note: Perspective API uses specific attribute names.
    # We'll request scores for common categories and map them later.
    requested_attributes = {
        "TOXICITY": {},
        "SEVERE_TOXICITY": {},
        "IDENTITY_ATTACK": {},
        "INSULT": {},
        "PROFANITY": {},
        "SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT": {},
        "FLIRTATION": {},
        "THREAT": {},
        "ATTACK_ON_COMMENTER": {},
        "ATTACK_ON_CIVILITY": {},
    }

    payload = {
        "comment": {"text": text_content},
        "requestedAttributes": requested_attributes,
        "doNotStore": True, # Privacy setting: tells API not to store the text
        "languages": ["en"] # Specify language if known, or omit for auto-detect
    }

    headers = {
        "Content-Type": "application/json"
    }

    params = {
        "key": api_key
    }

    response = requests.post(analyze_url, headers=headers, params=params, json=payload)
    response.raise_for_status()
    analysis_results = response.json()

    # Map Perspective API attribute names to a more generic structure and apply thresholds
    # This mapping is approximate and depends on the specific categories you're interested in
    # from the Perspective API output.
    # For this example, we'll map 'TOXICITY' to a generic 'harm' category,
    # and check other specific categories if they exist in category_thresholds.
    
    # A simple mapping for common safety concerns
    perspective_category_map = {
        "TOXICITY": "toxicity",
        "SEVERE_TOXICITY": "severe_toxicity",
        "IDENTITY_ATTACK": "identity_attack",
        "INSULT": "insult",
        "PROFANITY": "profanity",
        "SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT": "sexually_explicit",
        "THREAT": "threat",
    }

    for generic_category, threshold in category_thresholds.items():
        perspective_attr = None
        # Find the corresponding Perspective API attribute
        for key, value in perspective_category_map.items():
            if value == generic_category:
                perspective_attr = key
                break
        
        if perspective_attr and perspective_attr in analysis_results.get("attributeScores", {}):
            score = analysis_results["attributeScores"][perspective_attr]["summaryScore"]["value"]
            if score >= threshold:
                return False # Content exceeds threshold for this category

    return True
